en.html:
Fudaraku Castle. Still I could not get near it.

First, squeeze between the forces attacking it. That itself was no small difficulty.
Then cross the wall without anyone inside noticing. Arre, the first difficulty was only the welcome mat.

The night, also, was not going to hide me out of kindness.
In peacetime, perhaps. But this was war, and they were watching for night attacks. Getting in after dark was even more troublesome than in daylight.

Plainly speaking, I could neither do this nor do that. Completely stuck.

ja.html:
普陀楽城にはやはり近付けなかった。

　城を攻めている軍勢の隙間を縫うことからして容易
ではない。
　城壁を、中の兵に気付かれず越えるのは更に難しい。

　夜陰に乗じて忍び込むのも無理だった。
　平時ならいざ知らず今は戦時、夜襲を警戒している
ため昼間よりも厄介なほど。

　有体に言って、手も足も出ない。

en.html:
Long ago, Grandfather and Mother had taken me to see several battlefields.
So the situation, roughly I could understand.

This castle was about to fall.

In the confusion when it fell, I could probably slip inside.
…Getting inside only, that much would surely be easy.

But then find one person in all that turmoil? No, that would surely be impossible. A needle dropped into a raging sea, and I would be going to fetch it.

Before the castle fell. I had to find a way before that.
Into the castle, and to Kageaki.

ja.html:
昔、祖父と母とに連れられていくつもの戦場を見て
回ったことがある。
　だから、何となく情勢は察せられた。

　この城は落ちようとしている。

　落城の混乱に紛れ込めば、侵入は果たせるだろう。
　……侵入だけなら、簡単に違いない。

　しかし、その渦中で一人の人間を探すのは、きっと
不可能だ。
　荒れ狂う海に落とした針を拾いにゆくのと同じこと
になる。

　城が落ちる前に手立てを考えなくてはならないのだ。
　城内に入り、景明と会う手立てを。

en.html:
The curfew had been relaxed.
Going home was allowed. For some special errand outside, explain yourself to a patrol and get a permit. That was what the broadcast had announced a little earlier.

They were winning, so perhaps permission was becoming easier to give.
Whatever the reason, at least moving through town was easier now.

　自宅への帰宅は許可。何か特別な用事があって外出
したい者は巡回の兵士に事情を話して証明書をもらう
こと。……という放送が、先刻あった。

　彼らが勝ちつつあることと無関係ではあるまい。
　ともかくもそのお陰で、町の中での行動はしやすく
なっている。

en.html:
I thought of the soldiers I had just passed.
Their language, not a word I understood. The faces and the tone, though—haan, those explained enough.

Victory was almost theirs, so probably their heads were swelling along with their confidence.
Let them swell. I had no time for them.

Somewhere there had to be a way of getting close to the castle. I had to find it—

I kept running through Kamakura.

ja.html:
たった今すれ違った兵士の印象を思う。
　彼らの使う言語はさっぱりわからないが、顔と口調
で大体の意味は察せられた。

　勝利を目前にして、気が大きくなっているのだろう。
　構ってはいられない。

　どうにかして、城へ近付ける所を探さないと――

　私は鎌倉の町を走り続けた。
